slides.text: November 25, 1933. Gandhi returns to Dhamtari — the city where he had stood on Omar Seth's shoulders in 1920, where the Kandel Satyagraha had triumphed, where 15,000 had gathered at Makai Chowk. Thirteen years later. The same city. A different mission.
slides.visualDescription: Title card: Dhamtari 1933 — the same Makai Chowk, but thirteen years older. The crowd assembled for Gandhi's return. The ghost of 1920 visible in the same streets, the same buildings, different faces. A return as its own kind of beginning. Warm, documentary tone.

slides.text: In 1920, Gandhi came to Dhamtari to honour the Kandel Satyagraha — to support the farmers who had refused a false water tax. In 1933, he comes to fight untouchability. The city that received the political Gandhi now receives the social Gandhi.
slides.visualDescription: The contrast between 1920 and 1933 Dhamtari — the same streets but different purpose. 1920: farmers and canal rights. 1933: Harijans and temple doors. The same city, the same man, two different battles being fought with the same weapon: organised truth.

slides.text: Babu Chhotelal Srivastava — the organiser of the 1920 Kandel Satyagraha, the man Gandhi had named before 15,000 people — was at the 1933 Dhamtari meeting. Thirteen years had not diminished him. He was still here. Still committed. Still Dhamtari's conscience.
slides.visualDescription: Babu Chhotelal Srivastava in 1933 — older now, but the same quality of quiet determination. Receiving Gandhi in Dhamtari for the second time. Gandhi recognising him. The reunion of two people who share the 1920 Kandel moment as a defining memory.

slides.text: Narayan Rao Meghawale — who had co-led the Kandel Satyagraha and been imprisoned alongside Pt. Sharma — was also there. The man who made salt in Dhamtari during the 1930 Salt March echo. Thirteen years of sustained commitment in one face.
slides.visualDescription: Narayan Rao Meghawale in 1933 Dhamtari — the man who led the Kandel Satyagraha, who made salt in 1930, who was imprisoned alongside Sharma. His face showing thirteen years of the movement. Undiminished. The continuity of Dhamtari's resistance made human.

slides.text: Dhamtari's Harijan community — present at the 1933 meeting as they had not been at the 1920 meeting. The second visit deliberately included those who had been at the margins even of the freedom movement. Gandhi insisting that the movement belonged to everyone.
slides.visualDescription: The 1933 Dhamtari meeting with Harijan families prominently present — seated near the front rather than at the back. Their presence deliberate, structured. Gandhi having specifically asked for them to be included. The movement expanding to contain those it had partially excluded.

slides.text: Gandhi visited the Kandel village itself on November 25. The canal that had been the subject of the 1920 Satyagraha still flowed. The paddy still grew. The tax was still withdrawn — thirteen years later, the victory still intact. Gandhi came to see it with his own eyes.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi arriving at Kandel village — standing at the canal bank that was the subject of the 1920 Satyagraha. The water flowing freely. The paddy fields around it. Gandhi looking at the canal. The evidence of a permanent victory. Thirteen years and it still holds.

slides.text: The farmers of Kandel who had stood firm in August 1920 — some of them elderly now, some having passed on — were represented by their sons and grandsons. The Satyagraha they had waged was thirteen years old and still the defining moment of their village's identity.
slides.visualDescription: The farmers of Kandel in 1933 — the 1920 Satyagrahis now elderly, some represented by their sons who were infants in 1920. Gandhi meeting them at the canal bank. The canal as witness to the meeting between the past and the present of this victory.

slides.text: At Kandel, Gandhi specifically asked about the Harijan families of the village. Had the victory of the canal Satyagraha included them equally? Had their lives improved? The political victory and the social question — always inseparable for Gandhi.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi asking about Kandel's Harijans — the Satyagraha farmers slightly uncomfortable with the question. Some of the canal victory's beneficiaries had been Harijan farmers too. But caste remained. Gandhi noting: political victory is not enough. Social victory must follow.

slides.text: The Dhamtari meeting — held at the same Makai Chowk where Omar Seth had carried Gandhi on his shoulders in 1920. The physical space carrying thirteen years of memory. The crowd assembled again. This time without Omar Seth's act being needed — there was a stage.
slides.visualDescription: Makai Chowk, November 25, 1933 — the same space as December 21, 1920. The stage now properly prepared. Gandhi ascending it normally. The memory of Omar Seth's shoulders hanging in the air as context. Thirteen years of improvement: now there is a proper approach.

slides.text: Gandhi's speech at Makai Chowk in 1933: he remembered 1920 explicitly. He asked: how many of you were here thirteen years ago? Many hands went up. He said: you have not been idle in those thirteen years. What you have done here is why I came back.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi at the Makai Chowk podium in 1933 — asking who was there in 1920. Hands going up across the crowd. Gandhi acknowledging them. His gratitude: you kept the movement alive without me. You are the reason I came back. The crowd moved by being seen.

slides.text: The Harijan Sevak Sangh collection at the 1933 Dhamtari meeting — generous, immediate, from a city that had already proven its willingness to give. The same impulse that put Rs 501 in the Tilak Fund in 1920 now filling the Harijan Fund in 1933.
slides.visualDescription: The Harijan Sevak Sangh collection at Dhamtari 1933 — the same generosity as 1920 but for a different cause. Bajirao Kridatta's family perhaps contributing again. The city of Dhamtari giving twice to two different aspects of the same freedom.

slides.text: Gandhi visited the homes of Harijan families in Dhamtari. Sitting with them in their quarters. Eating with them. Listening to their daily realities — what untouchability cost them, what they hoped for, what they had been told about themselves that was not true.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi in the Harijan quarters of Dhamtari — sitting on the ground in a modest home. The Harijan family around him. Gandhi listening as they describe their daily reality under untouchability. The Mahatma as witness to the ordinary violence of caste.

slides.text: A Harijan woman in Dhamtari told Gandhi: 'We were told that your shadow would pollute us too.' Gandhi looked at the shadow he cast and said: 'My shadow and yours fall on the same ground. The same earth receives us both.' The shadow as theology.
slides.visualDescription: A Harijan woman's testimony to Gandhi in Dhamtari — her words about shadow pollution. Gandhi looking at the ground where his shadow and hers both fall. His response: the same earth receives both. The ground as the ultimate democracy. Shadow as argument.

slides.text: The Dhamtari visit also included the Satnam Ashram vicinity — the community that Pt. Sundarlal Sharma had built between Raipur and Dhamtari. Gandhi revisited to see again what had moved him: a community of equals, functioning, permanent.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi at the Satnam Ashram community in the Dhamtari vicinity — the community of equals that Sharma built. Gandhi walking through it again, speaking with residents. The living proof of his mission. The ashram as evidence that the world he was fighting for already existed somewhere.

slides.text: Abbas Bhai — the transport operator who had driven Gandhi to Dhamtari in 1920 and lost his license for it — was remembered at the 1933 meeting. Someone mentioned his name. Gandhi asked after him. The movement's memory reaching back to honour those who paid the ordinary prices.
slides.visualDescription: At the 1933 Dhamtari meeting — someone mentions Abbas Bhai. Gandhi asking after him. The story of the canceled transport license told again. Gandhi's face: the expression of a man who carries the weight of what ordinary people paid for extraordinary causes.

slides.text: What happened to Abbas Bhai after his license was cancelled? He found other work. He did not leave the movement. He was at the 1933 meeting — older, without his Raipur Bus Service, but still completely committed. The cancellation had not broken him.
slides.visualDescription: Abbas Bhai at the 1933 Dhamtari meeting — without his transport company, but present. The man who lost his business for Gandhi's journey now present at Gandhi's return. Thirteen years and the commitment unchanged. The business gone. The man whole.

slides.text: The evening of November 25 in Dhamtari — a smaller gathering, more intimate than the Makai Chowk meeting. Gandhi sitting with the Congress workers, the freedom fighters, the people who had been in this from before 1920. A family reunion of the movement.
slides.visualDescription: The intimate evening gathering in Dhamtari — Gandhi with the core movement workers. Not the public crowd of Makai Chowk but the inner circle: Srivastava, Meghawale, the Satyagraha veterans. A smaller room, bigger honesty. The movement family together.

slides.text: Gandhi asked the Dhamtari workers to tell him what they had done since 1920 — each person accounting for thirteen years. The accounts: national school, Jungle Satyagraha, salt-making in 1930, Harijan work, continued Congress organising. Thirteen years of full commitment.
slides.visualDescription: The evening meeting — each Dhamtari freedom fighter giving account of their thirteen years. Gandhi listening to each. Srivastava: the canal victory, then Harijan work. Meghawale: the Kandel co-leadership, then salt-making, then continued organising. Gandhi listening to what his name had continued without him.

slides.text: Gandhi was moved by what he heard. He said to the Dhamtari workers: 'The movement has been in good hands here. You have not waited for me to come. You have acted. That is the only proof that Satyagraha has truly taken root — when it acts without the Satyagrahi.'
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi speaking to the Dhamtari workers after hearing their accounts. His words visible: the movement has been in good hands. The workers receiving this not as praise but as confirmation. They knew they had acted. Gandhi seeing it is the completion of the act.

slides.text: The circle from 1920 to 1933 in Dhamtari: the Kandel canal victory, the national school, the Jungle Satyagraha, the salt-making, the continued Congress work, and now Gandhi's return. Each event a link in a chain. Each link held by a different pair of hands.
slides.visualDescription: The chain of Dhamtari's thirteen years — visualised as actual links: the Kandel canal, the school, the Jungle Satyagraha, the salt, the Congress meetings. Each link a different colour, connected to the next. The chain leading to Gandhi's return in 1933.

slides.text: November 25, 1933 draws to a close in Dhamtari. Gandhi will move to the village circuits tomorrow — Tamora, Devri, Kurud. But first: one more meeting in Dhamtari at dawn, a smaller gathering, a prayer, a sending-off.
slides.visualDescription: The end of November 25 in Dhamtari — the day complete. Gandhi at prayer in the early morning before the next day's village circuits. The quiet of Dhamtari at dawn. The small gathering for the dawn prayer. The movement in its most intimate form: a man praying.

slides.text: The 1920 memory of Makai Chowk lived in Dhamtari's collective identity. The city had built its sense of itself around that December day in 1920 — around Omar Seth's act, around Gandhi's hour-long speech, around the 500 who went to Nagpur. The memory as civic pride.
slides.visualDescription: Dhamtari's collective memory of 1920 — the images that the city carries in its identity. Makai Chowk. Omar Seth. The 500 for Nagpur. The Tilak Fund bag. The hour-long speech. These are the civic foundation stones. Gandhi's return in 1933 adding to them.

slides.text: The return to Dhamtari was also a return to where the relationship between Gandhi and Chhattisgarh had been most dramatically enacted. If Raipur was the arrival and the platform, Dhamtari was the heart — where the Satyagraha had been, where the crowd had been densest.
slides.visualDescription: Dhamtari as the heart of Gandhi's Chhattisgarh relationship — the city where the Kandel Satyagraha happened, where Omar Seth lifted him, where the 500 committed to Nagpur. Raipur was the capital; Dhamtari was the soul. Both necessary. Both loved.

slides.text: The Dhamtari of 1933 also had new leaders — a second generation of movement workers, younger people who had grown up with the 1920 visit as their formative story. They had not been at Makai Chowk in 1920 — they had heard about it at their parents' knees.
slides.visualDescription: The second generation of Dhamtari's freedom movement — young adults in 1933 who were children in 1920. They received Gandhi not as their own first encounter but as the fulfillment of a story they had been told. The 1920 visit as their inherited mythology, now made real.

slides.text: Gandhi looked at the young faces and said: you are the proof that the work continues. The old generation will not be here forever. You are the reason the movement will. The succession of commitment — one generation receiving from another — as the deepest form of victory.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi looking at the young Dhamtari workers — second generation, fresh faces carrying inherited commitment. His words to them: you are the proof. The movement's continuity made human in their faces. The old guard passing to the young guard in the presence of Gandhi.

slides.text: The Kandel canal: still flowing. The national school: still teaching. The Congress committee: still meeting. The Harijan families: still waiting for full inclusion. The movement's victories and the movement's unfinished work visible side by side in one city.
slides.visualDescription: Dhamtari in November 1933 — its victories and its unfinished work side by side. The canal flowing free: victory. The national school teaching: victory. The Harijan quarter still at the margin: unfinished. Both truths visible, both acknowledged. The work half done.

slides.text: Gandhi said to Dhamtari: you have a debt to the Harijans. The Kandel Satyagraha won the canal for the farmers — all the farmers, including the Harijan farmers. Did the Harijan farmers receive their share of the victory? The question that requires a true answer.
slides.visualDescription: Gandhi asking Dhamtari the hard question: the Kandel victory benefited all farmers. Did the Harijan farmers receive their share? The silence in the room. The movement workers looking at each other. The honest answer: partly. Gandhi: then the Satyagraha is not yet complete.

slides.text: The Dhamtari movement workers accepted the challenge. They promised Gandhi: we will work on untouchability with the same discipline we brought to the Kandel Satyagraha. The method proven. Now applying it to the older, deeper injustice.
slides.visualDescription: The Dhamtari workers accepting Gandhi's challenge — nodding, committing, some speaking aloud their commitment. The method of the Kandel Satyagraha applied now to untouchability. The same discipline, the same organisation, the same non-violence. A new application.

slides.text: November 25, 1933. The return to Dhamtari complete. Tomorrow: the village circuits — Tamora, Devri, Kurud. The day after: departure from Raipur. These are Gandhi's last two days in Chhattisgarh. He does not know this. The land does not know this. History keeps its own counsel.
slides.visualDescription: The end of November 25 — Gandhi's last full day in Dhamtari. The city quiet around him. Two more days of Chhattisgarh remain. Tomorrow: village circuits. The day after: departure. Neither Gandhi nor Chhattisgarh knowing these are the final hours.

slides.text: The return to Dhamtari was a closing of a circle. The canal that brought Gandhi in 1920, the Satyagraha that won before he arrived, the shoulders that carried him through the crowd — all of it gathered into the 1933 return. The circle complete. The account balanced.
slides.visualDescription: The full circle of Gandhi and Dhamtari — 1920 arrival, 1920 Makai Chowk, 1930 Jungle Satyagraha, 1933 return. A visual circle drawing these four points together. The relationship between Gandhi and Dhamtari as its own complete story within the larger story.

slides.text: Babu Chhotelal Srivastava — the first Satyagrahi of Kandel, the man Gandhi named in 1920, the man present in 1933 — represents everything the freedom movement was: local, unglamorous, sustained, disciplined, and ultimately effective.
slides.visualDescription: Portrait of Babu Chhotelal Srivastava in 1933 — the same face as 1920 but older. At the center of Dhamtari's 1933 meeting. He did not become famous. He did not leave Dhamtari. He stayed and continued. The movement's most essential character: the one who stays.

slides.text: The Kandel canal still flows through its village today. No monument marks the Kandel Satyagraha. No national history book records Srivastava's name. But the water is free, and the paddy grows, and the Satyagraha of 1920 holds its victory intact across a century.
slides.visualDescription: Present-day Kandel — the canal flowing, the paddy growing, the village at peace. No monument. No plaque. No national recognition. Only the water, only the paddy, only the permanent victory of the men and women who refused a false tax in August 1920.

slides.text: Omar Seth of Gurur — the man who carried Gandhi on his shoulders through Makai Chowk in 1920 — is not in any history book. The Dhamtari city he lived in carries his act in its collective memory. The act immortal. The man unknown nationally. Known locally forever.
slides.visualDescription: The site of Omar Seth's act at Makai Chowk, Dhamtari — the same ground in 1933 and today. No monument to the businessman from Gurur who lifted Gandhi above the crowd. But in Dhamtari's memory: the act is known. The local immortality of an unrecorded hero.

slides.text: The return to Dhamtari was Gandhi's gift to the city — acknowledgement that he remembered, that what happened here in 1920 mattered, that he came back. The city's gift to Gandhi was its thirteen years of continued work. An exchange of remembering.
slides.visualDescription: The exchange between Gandhi and Dhamtari — Gandhi's return as his gift of remembering; Dhamtari's thirteen years as its gift to Gandhi. Two forms of fidelity meeting in Makai Chowk in November 1933. An exchange between equals who honour each other.

slides.text: November 25, 1933 in Dhamtari. The last time Gandhi will stand in this city. The last time Srivastava will see him. The last time Meghawale will speak with him. The last time the 1920 Kandel veterans will be in his physical presence. The last time, not yet known.
slides.visualDescription: The ending of the Dhamtari day — Gandhi's last evening in this city, though none know it yet. The goodbyes warm but not final in tone. See you when you come back. Gandhi accepting this. History silent about what it knows. The last evening of the last full Chhattisgarh visit.

slides.text: Tomorrow: the village circuits of November 26-27. Tamora, Devri, Kurud — the villages where the movement had taken root most deeply, where the ordinary people most needed Gandhi's presence, where the Harijan work was most needed and most possible.
slides.visualDescription: The village circuits of November 26-27 being previewed — Tamora, Devri, Kurud on the map. The rural heartland of the Chhattisgarh movement. Where the work is least visible and most essential. Gandhi preparing to go to the places that the cities cannot reach.

slides.text: The return to Dhamtari: complete. The circle: closed. Tomorrow: the villages — where the real India lives, and where Gandhi always found the real movement. Next: Episode 6 — The Village Circuit.
slides.visualDescription: Dhamtari at night — quiet, complete, carrying its November 25 in its memory. Gandhi's motor resting. Tomorrow's road already visible in the moonlight — heading toward Tamora, Devri, Kurud. The villages waiting. Title card: Episode 6 — The Village Circuit.
